children.why_this_cut: The first section (letter_and_spirit) is self-contained: it covers interpretation of instructions, detecting conflicts, and examples. The only cross-link is the chain_of_command concept (seeded) used in the no_other_objectives section, which is in the second child.

The remaining sections (no_other_objectives, scope_of_autonomy, control_side_effects) are cohesive around autonomy and side effects. The only cross-link is the chain_of_command concept (seeded) used in the no_other_objectives section, which is in the second child.

judgment_calls: Cut at L425 (end of letter_and_spirit section) rather than at L460 (end of no_other_objectives) because the letter_and_spirit section is a self-contained unit; the no_other_objectives section shares the chain_of_command dependency with the later sections, so grouping it with them keeps the cross-link surface minimal.
The scope_of_autonomy concept is seeded from L461-488, which is entirely within child 2, so it is not a cross-link; child 2 will need to provide it internally.
The stay_in_bounds_content_categories and transformation_exception seeds are not present in this span; they are not carried forward.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, and the mechanism for identifying and following applicable instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: candidate_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: all instructions in the Model Spec plus unquoted plain text in system, developer, and user messages, each assigned the authority level of its containing section or message

seed_vocabulary.name: applicable_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: candidate instructions that are not misaligned with a higher-level instruction, superseded by a later same-level instruction, or suspected to be mistaken

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user, defining which sub-goals may be pursued, acceptable side effects, and when to pause for clarification
